title: Club 51 Sports Bar scores big with fans during Kitchener Rangers home opener
content: Kitchener, ON – Hundreds of hockey fans got their first game-day experience at Club 51 Sports Bar during the Kitchener Rangers' home opener last Friday, marking a strong start for the new sports bar and gathering space at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium (The Aud).

The successful opening followed a sneak peek celebration held earlier in the week, where members of the media, City council, staff, project partners and construction teams gathered for a ribbon cutting and first look at the transformed space. The event recognized the work that went into converting the former Subscribers Lounge into a modern restaurant and community gathering place inside The Aud.

"For 75 years, The Aud has been one of Kitchener's most beloved gathering places," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “In May 2025, our Council approved $2M to bring in a vibrant dining space for concert goers, sports fans and residents. I'm proud of the innovative projects we’ve taken on, like Club 51, that show how thoughtful investments can honour a facility’s history while creating new experiences that meet the needs of today's residents and visitors.”
Hometown hospitality

Designed to serve guests year-round, Club 51 offers elevated pub fare, local craft beverages and a strong focus on supporting local suppliers and producers throughout Waterloo Region. In addition to game-day offerings, Club 51 will welcome fans in for Rangers’ away game streaming and other event opportunities.

Matt and Jackie Rolleman, owners and operators of Club 51 Sports Bar, said the vision was to create a welcoming destination that reflects the energy and history of The Aud while delivering a premium hospitality experience.

"Seeing the restaurant come to life during the Rangers' home opener was incredibly rewarding," said Jackie Rolleman, co-owner of Club 51. "We were proud to welcome so many people from across the community. Fans arrived early, families stayed for dinner and people took the time to enjoy the space. The turnout showed us just how much people value having another place to gather at The Aud."
For reservations, menus and operating hours, visit Club 51 Sports Bar's website . Find tickets for games, events and concerts at The Aud on KitchenerLIVE.ca .
About The Aud

Since opening in 1951, The Aud has served as one of Kitchener's premier entertainment and community venues, hosting sporting events, concerts, exhibitions, family programming and community celebrations. In 2026, The Aud celebrates its 75th anniversary.
About Club 51 Sports Bar

Owned and operated by The Rolleman Group, Club 51 Sports Bar is a modern take on the classic sports bar, proudly located inside the historic Kitchener Memorial Auditorium. Named after the year The Aud opened in 1951, Club 51 blends the rich history of this iconic venue with elevated pub fare, local craft beer, Ontario-made beverages, and warm hospitality.
Club 51 Sports Bar proudly continues the tradition of bringing community and sport together in one place.
For more information:  Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener media@kitchener.ca

title: King StrEATery Food Truck Festival highlights 50 local businesses in Downtown Kitchener this Sunday
content: Kitchener is celebrating local businesses, entrepreneurs and artisans with the re-launch of Downtown Kitchener's popular King StrEATery Food Truck Festival this Sunday, September 27 from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. on King Street East (from Eby to Cedar Street), at the Kitchener Market piazza and many east end businesses.

King StrEATery, a vibrant, pedestrian-friendly celebration, will bring together 50 participating local businesses, including 15 food trucks, as well as food vendors, east end shops and cafes, and a Love Local Artisan Market for a day of food, shopping and community in the heart of downtown.
Browse one-of-a-kind goods at the Love Local Artisan Market featuring more than 15 local entrepreneurs and artisans and explore the shops and businesses of Kitchener’s east end.

Along with great food and shopping, visitors can enjoy Drew Ripley’s Big Balloon Show, buskers, giant games, free dance lessons (K-Pop, salsa and line dancing with TenC Dance Co.) and relax in the licensed outdoor bar area.

Admission is free, and free Sunday parking is available, including at the Kitchener Market parking garage. Visitors are also encouraged to bring a non-perishable food donation for The Food Bank of Waterloo Region .
For the full list of food trucks, food vendors, Love Local Artisan Market and participating east end businesses, visit DowntownKitchener.ca/KingStreatery.

title: Kitchener expands strategic plan engagement through international partnership with Google Jigsaw and Make.org
content: KITCHENER, ON — The City of Kitchener is building on its longstanding commitment to community engagement by launching a new initiative that will help more residents contribute to the development of the City's 2027-2030 Strategic Plan.

As one of a small number of global municipalities selected for the Google Jigsaw Partners Program , Kitchener will leverage Sensemaking, an innovative engagement approach that helps policymakers gather and interpret thousands of individual perspectives into clear, actionable insights. The City joins international Partners Program members such as Gdańsk, Poland; Schenectady, New York; Riverside, California; and Houston, Texas, in advancing innovative, technology-enabled approaches to community engagement. The initiative will complement Kitchener’s existing strategic planning engagement, which has already connected with more than 1,500 residents through a survey, workshops, community conversations and other outreach activities.

The partnership reflects Kitchener's culture of innovation and technology, including its status as the home of Google's Canadian engineering headquarters, while reinforcing the City's commitment to ensuring technology serves people and strengthens civic participation.

"The City of Kitchener is proud to be chosen as a Google Jigsaw partner.  Kitchener has a strong record of putting community voices at the centre of decision-making and our Strategic Plan is one of the most important opportunities for residents to help shape the future of our city," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "Many of our neighbours, colleagues, and friends have already contributed ideas and feedback. This opportunity allows us to build on that momentum, hear from more residents and gain deeper insights that will help shape Kitchener's future."

Google’s community engagement platform partner will support the initiative, Make.org, an independent civic technology organization that specializes in large-scale public participation and democratic engagement. Make.org has engaged millions of participants globally through its consultation platform.

Sensemaking technology will help the City explore important topics in greater depth by capturing insights that go beyond responses to pre-set questions. This AI-supported approach can provide richer insights than traditional surveys. This engagement opportunity is expected to launch before the end of 2026. Residents can learn more about the strategic plan and upcoming engagement opportunities at engagewr.ca/kitchenerstrategicplan .
For more information Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener Media@kitchener.ca

title: Square Peg Winter Pop-up set to showcase local business in the heart of downtown
content: Downtown Kitchener shoppers can look forward to discovering a new lineup of local retailers this holiday season as the Square Peg Winter Pop-up returns to City Hall’s doorstep.

Beginning in November, Square Peg, the City of Kitchener’s retail incubator space at 220 King St. W., will be transformed into a bustling holiday marketplace featuring local products, handmade goods, and emerging brands. From November 16, 2026, to January 1, 2027, visitors will find a fresh and festive shopping experience throughout the holiday season.

The pop-up supports local entrepreneurship while contributing to a vibrant downtown experience during the holiday season. The initiative provides emerging retailers with an opportunity to test new concepts, reach new customers and gain experience operating in one of Kitchener’s busiest commercial areas. Each participating business will activate its own dedicated nook within the space, alongside several other retailers, creating a vibrant marketplace featuring a variety of local products and brands.

The City of Kitchener offers the Winter Pop-up to help local businesses grow while creating a unique shopping experience that attracts residents and visitors to downtown Kitchener during the holiday season.

Interested retailers can apply online until September 30, 2026 using the City of Kitchener’s application form . Additional information and eligibility criteria is available within the form to help retailers prepare their application.
For more information on everything there is to experience in Downtown Kitchener, contact downtown@kitchener.ca or visit DowntownKitchener.ca.
About Square Peg

Square Peg is a high-visibility, community-focused pop-up retail space in downtown Kitchener that gives  independent retailers and emerging entrepreneurs the opportunity to showcase their products, test new concepts and connect with customers in a real storefront environment.

title: Passing of Otis the swan
content: We are deeply saddened to share that Otis, one of Victoria Park’s beloved swans, passed away peacefully during the evening of September 18, 2026. He was approximately 19 years old.
Otis has been a familiar and much-loved presence at Victoria Park since his arrival in 2009. He brought joy to countless visitors and helped create special memories for many people in our community.

His mate, Ophelia, remains in Victoria Park under close observation, and we are working with a veterinarian to support her through this transition. We ask visitors to continue giving Ophelia space and treating her with care and respect.
Otis was predeceased by his first mate, Snowy, as well as a cygnet.
We know this news will be very difficult for the many people who came to know and care for Otis. We are grateful for the community’s kindness and care for both swans.

title: Culture Days kicks off with free arts, music and creative experiences across Kitchener
content: Culture Days has arrived in Kitchener, bringing together artists, performers, arts organizations and community members for a celebration of creativity and connection. This province-wide celebration of arts, creativity and heritage runs from September 18 to October 4, with a wide range of free events, performances, exhibitions, workshops and tours taking place across the city.

As part of this celebration, the City of Kitchener is hosting a kick-off weekend from September 25 to 27 featuring live music, film screening, songwriting workshop, artist talks, and arts hub open house and street-level creativity at Gaukel Block, and so much more. title: Celebrate Kitchener's Urban Forest at the First Forestry Fall Fair
content: Residents of all ages are invited to explore the city's urban forest at Kitchener's first Forestry Fall Fair on Saturday, September 26 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Huron Natural Area.

The event will feature crafts and family-friendly activities, face painting, self-guided nature walks and opportunities to discover the important role trees and natural areas play in creating a healthy, sustainable community.

City of Kitchener staff from Forestry and Natural Areas, Stormwater and Sanitary Utilities, and the Neighbourhood Development Office will be joined by representatives of local community organizations including REEP Green Solutions, the Region of Waterloo, Grand River Conservation Authority, Kitchener Nature Stewards and Bird-friendly Kitchener to provide more in-depth information to visitors.
Whether you're a nature enthusiast, a curious learner or looking for a fun family outing, the Forestry Fall Fair offers something for everyone.
For more information, visit Kitchener.ca/ForestryFair

title: Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park opens November 14, expanding sport, recreation and active living access for a community in motion
content: The City of Kitchener will officially open the new Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park on Saturday, November 14, creating more opportunities for residents of all ages and abilities to connect, compete, and belong through sport, recreation and community experiences. Community members are invited to join the grand opening ceremony and stay for family-focused activities throughout the day.   As the largest capital project in the City’s history, the centre is designed to respond to the needs of a growing and changing community by expanding access to indoor sport and recreation opportunities, while creating a welcoming place for people to get active, spend time together and build connections with others. Located in RBJ Schlegel Park, the centre is expected to bring the community together with more than 500,000 visits in the first year alone, and provide additional training, practice and competition space for dozens of local sport organizations.

"The opening of Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park is one of the most significant investments in community infrastructure in Kitchener's history," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "This facility will help more children learn to swim, give families more opportunities to be active together, provide welcoming spaces for residents of all abilities, and bring people together through sport, recreation and community events."

The centre includes a quad gymnasium, FIFA-sized indoor turf field that can be divided into four playing areas, two cricket practice nets, competition and leisure pools, and an indoor walking track. Together, these spaces will support a wide variety of sports like basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, cricket, futsal, pickleball, badminton and swimming.   For local sport organizations, this additional space will create opportunities to expand programs, accommodate more participants and help reduce waitlists. For residents, it means more chances to discover a new activity, or to continue playing a sport they already enjoy.   “We’re incredibly excited to welcome the community into the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park,” said Michael May, Deputy Chief Administrative Officer for the City of Kitchener. "From the very beginning, this facility has been designed with the people who will use it most top of mind: players, families, fans, coaches, partners and volunteers. Whether someone is attending their first swim lesson, playing in a basketball tournament, walking the indoor track or cheering on a family member, we want their experience to be welcoming, accessible and enjoyable."
More than a sports facility, the Cowan Recreation Centre is designed as a community gathering space that will create lasting benefits for the entire community:

More opportunities to stay active – The Cowan Recreation Centre expands Kitchener's indoor recreation options, providing more diverse opportunities for residents to participate in more sport, recreation and physical activity opportunities year-round.

Accessible for everyone  – Designed to meet the highest standards of any City facility, the centre features ramp access to both pools, wider pathways, guiding floor textures and accessible viewing areas, making it easier for people of all ages and abilities to participate, watch and connect with others.

Built for sustainability  – As the City's first net-zero carbon building and one of Canada's most sustainable municipally owned recreation facilities, the centre includes rooftop solar power generation, geothermal energy, mass timber construction, stainless steel pools, stormwater management and a green roof.

A venue for major events – Built to host provincial and national competitions, tournaments and events, the centre will showcase Kitchener, support local businesses and generate millions of dollars in economic activity, while giving local athletes the opportunity to compete closer to home.

On November 14, residents are invited to celebrate the official opening of the Cowan Recreation Centre, located in the heart of RBJ Schlegel Park (1664 Huron Road). Beginning at 9 a.m. , the free community event will feature something for all ages, including an official ribbon-cutting ceremony, guided tours of the facility, free public swims and sport activities, family-friendly entertainment including bouncy castles and face painters, equipment demonstrations, giveaways, prizes and activities throughout the day. The day's programming schedule will be published closer to the event.

To stay up-to-date on grand opening details, future programming and amenities, and more, visit the City's newly launched RBJ Schlegel Park webpage which includes detailed information about the Cowan Recreation Centre – Kitchener.ca/RBJSchlegelPark

title: Welcoming Week event connects newcomers with community supports
content: KITCHENER, ON  – Earlier this week, more than 150 people gathered at Kitchener City Hall to attend the launch of the City of Kitchener's first Municipal Newcomer Strategy and mark the beginning of Welcoming Week. The Council-approved strategy provides a coordinated approach to help newcomers access information, services and opportunities, strengthen their sense of belonging and fully participate in Kitchener community life.

Developed through extensive community engagement, the Municipal Newcomer Strategy was informed by more than 1,000 newcomer voices, over 25 engagement activities and community-led events, collaboration with newcomer-serving organizations, and consultation with City staff and community partners. The strategy outlines 15 actions to be implemented over three years and is organized around five key themes: boosting awareness of City services, small business and employment supports, community belonging and connections, targeted supports for newcomers and equipping Team Kitchener to better serve newcomer communities.

"Kitchener's success as a progressive and welcoming community is strengthened by the people who choose to make our community their home," said Berry Vrbanovic, Mayor of Kitchener. "This strategy reflects what we heard directly from newcomers, service providers and community partners about the opportunities and challenges newcomers' experience when building a life in our city. By approving this strategy, Council has established a clear roadmap to help ensure newcomers feel welcomed, connected and supported as they establish their lives in Kitchener."

The Municipal Newcomer Strategy focuses on improving access to information and services, supporting economic participation, fostering community connections and strengthening organizational capacity across the corporation. One of the first actions completed through the strategy is the creation of the Welcome to Kitchener Newcomer Guide and enhanced online newcomer hub, which provide newcomers with a centralized place to access information about City services, community programs, recreation opportunities and local supports.

"Today's event reflects the collective efforts of many organizations, community partners and residents who helped shape this work," said Rumina Morris, Director, Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion. "Throughout engagement, we heard the importance of making information easier to find and helping newcomers feel connected and welcomed. The guide and online hub are important tools that support those goals."
Attendees had the opportunity to meet directly with organizations providing support related to settlement, employment, education, housing, language services, recreation and community connection.
Residents can learn more about the Municipal Newcomer Strategy and access the Newcomer Guide at kitchener.ca/Welcome .

title: Celebrate a season of gardening, growth and community at Kitchener in Bloom's end-of-season celebration
content: From colourful flower beds and thriving vegetable gardens to pollinator-friendly spaces, Kitchener residents have spent the growing season helping neighbourhoods bloom. Now, the community is invited to come together and celebrate those efforts at the City of Kitchener's Kitchener in Bloom End-of-Season Celebration.

Taking place on Thursday, September 24, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. at the Victoria Park Pavilion , this free community event will bring together gardeners, families and green space enthusiasts from across the city to connect, learn and celebrate another successful growing season.

Participants will have the opportunity to chat with local gardening organizations, listen to educational talks with horticultural experts, connect with other gardeners, enjoy family-friendly activities and enter prize draws. Light refreshments will also be available.

Kitchener in Bloom recognizes the important role residents play in beautifying neighbourhoods, supporting biodiversity and creating vibrant, welcoming green spaces throughout the city. Whether tending to a backyard garden, growing vegetables, planting native species or caring for a community garden plot, residents help make Kitchener a greener and more sustainable city.

The end-of-season celebration offers an opportunity to recognize these contributions while bringing together gardeners of all experience levels to share ideas, learn from one another and find inspiration for future growing seasons.
Residents are encouraged to reserve their spot in advance by registering through Eventbrite .
To learn more about Kitchener in Bloom and other neighbourhood greening initiatives, visit LoveMyHood.ca/bloom .
